title: Mainland south-east Australian catchments protected before 1997 lost about as much runoff after 1997 as unprotected ones; four wet Tasmanian catchments made the planned opposite result (175 basins)
abstract: Question: after 1997, runoff in 175 south-east Australian (SE-AU) catchments fell 12-16% below each catchment's 1951-1996 relation to rain and temperature and stayed low. Is human land and water use (farm dams, plantations, groundwater pumping, logging) necessary for this deficit? Approach: we calculated the area fraction of each catchment in CAPAD 2024 protected areas gazetted before 1997 and compared protected and other catchments with the annual model of campaign bundle 871b2192 (AGCD and SILO rain, cluster bootstrap). The analysis plan was written before any protected-area result. Results: in the planned test, the 18 catchments with 60% or more protected had almost no deficit in 2010-2021 (AGCD -3.6%, 95% CI -15.2 to +3.3; SILO +3.8%); the planned difference to agricultural catchments (+12.6 points, -10.5 to +31.1) was inconclusive. Post hoc checks showed that four very wet Tasmanian wilderness catchments made this result. After a fire adjustment (fire raises runoff; 15 of 18 protected catchments burned), the 14 mainland protected catchments were 18.7% below their relation (7.9-36.5%; 68 mm/yr), and the 145 mainland unprotected catchments 20.7% (14.2-27.8%). Aridity-limited neighbour matching gave a difference of +1.9 points (-8.2 to +10.4; SILO +0.7, -21.0 to +15.2). Regressions on protected fraction and on land-use and disturbance indices showed no land-use effect. Protected catchments also lost 19% of their rain sensitivity. Conclusion: on the mainland, human land and water use is not necessary for the deficit; with AGCD it explains at most about half. Four protected western Tasmanian catchments had no deficit while five nearby unprotected ones lost 7%; this is an open question. Limitations: the main conclusion depends on post hoc checks; small protected sample; SILO intervals are wide; CAPAD dates and fire coefficients are imperfect.
